chunks: Majority carriers in P-type vs N-type. The question: What charge carriers are dominant in P-type semiconductors vs N-type semiconductors?
The majority carrier is whichever carrier is plentiful in a doped semiconductor. In N-type material it is electrons. In P-type material it is holes.
The doping sets the majority count. The other type is still there, as the minority carrier, but in tiny numbers.
Both matter, because the minority carriers do the work inside diodes and transistors.
Picture a school where almost every student is a left-hander, with just a few right-handers. The left-handers are the majority, and they set the character of the school.
The few right-handers are still there, and in some situations, like a special club, they are the ones that matter.
The analogy undersells one thing: in silicon the ratio is extreme, often a million million to one.
Below N D about n i both carriers sit near n i and the material is effectively intrinsic.

Above it the majority tracks the doping (slope 1) while the minority falls as 1 over N D (slope -1); the two lines mirror each other about n i because np equals n i squared is a straight line of constant sum on a log scale.
The same plot applies to P-type with the roles swapped.
Majority carrier: the plentiful carrier, electrons in N-type, holes in P-type. Minority carrier: the scarce carrier.
Intrinsic density ( n i ): carrier density in pure silicon, about 10 to the 10 per cm³. Mass-action law: np equals n i squared , which links the two carrier densities.
Doping: adding impurities to set the carrier type.
Dope silicon N-type with 10 to the 16 donors per cm³. The electrons number about 10 to the 16 per cm³.
The mass-action law gives holes as n i squared over n equals 10 to the 20 over 10 to the 16 equals 10 to the 4 per cm³.
The two differ by a factor of 10 to the 12 , a million million. That is the whole idea.
"N-type has electrons as the majority carrier, P-type has holes. The majority density is about equal to the doping, say 10 to the 16 per cm³.
The minority carrier is set by np equals n i squared , so with n i equals 10 to the 10 it's only 10 to the 4 per cm³, twelve orders lower.
Majority carriers carry the bulk current, but minority carriers matter at junctions: they set diode and BJT current and reverse leakage."
